Hi Maria — thank you for the signal and the timeline. We're actively investigating. Initial summary: we are seeing elevated p95 in EU for short-sequence generation after a KV-cache eviction threshold change rolled earlier today; error rates remain low, but latency tail is higher for cached-heavy traffic patterns.

Immediate things we're doing for you:
- Moving your traffic to an alternate EU pool with conservative cache settings (expected within ~12 minutes).
- Re-routing any critical routes to the fallback model (smaller variant) if latency exceeds 700ms for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Engaging runtime engineering (cc'd) to look for regression and start a targeted rollback if mitigation isn't holding.

Can you confirm which hostnames/endpoints you rely on (we have orchida-prod and orchida-intake)? We'll prioritize orchida-prod.

I'll follow up with a short action checklist and timeline. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

— Lauren
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Action summary & next steps — Orchida EU latency incident (Oct 3)

Hi Maria / Orchida team —

Thanks again for flagging this and for patience while we completed the initial triage. Quick readout and next steps: 

What happened (short):
- On 2026-10-03 at ~08:40 UTC a runtime configuration change increased KV-cache eviction aggressiveness for eu pools. For customers with high short-prompt/low-seq distributions this produced elevated p95 while overall error rates stayed low.

What we did:
- Within 12 minutes we moved Orchida's traffic to an alternate EU pool configured with conservative cache retention.
- Enabled prefix pinning and a temporary route to a smaller model variant for requests that hit tail latency thresholds.
- Reverted the configuration change in the primary eu pool as of 10:02 UTC once we validated stability.

Customer impact:
- Intermittent p95 latency elevation for generation calls to orchida-prod in EU between ~08:40–10:05 UTC on 2026-10-03. Approximate affected window: 1h25m. No sustained 5xx spike observed.

Compensation and next steps: 
- We will apply a 10% service credit for October usage to the Orchida account as a good-faith gesture; Ben will coordinate details with your purchasing contact.
- Engineering has opened JIRA-RI-3492 to track the postmortem and the permanent fix (changes to the KV eviction policy and improved canary gating).
- We'll share a draft postmortem by Oct 8 and schedule a short review call (15–20 min) the following week to walk the timeline and technical root cause.

Immediate ask from Orchida: please confirm you received the mitigation and whether the application telemetry looks back to normal for your end. Also confirm the correct billing contact for credit (if different from purchasing@orchidahealth.com).

Attachments included: orchida_incident_timeline.csv, mitigation-checklist.pdf, proposed-credit-summary.txt

Apologies again for the disruption. We're prioritizing a permanent fix and will follow up with a full postmortem and timeline.

Best,
